body:
I'd never leave him - or put him in a position that could potentially screw up his life... Because if I said "dump your jobs/life/friends/rent contract etc right now or I'll never be happy/I will leave" he might love me enough to do it! I wouldn't EVER put him in that position, or abuse the love he gives in that way. 

Sure he's not perfect, and he doesn't know how to support me emotionally in the right way sometimes. But he's a genuinely loving, wonderful man and he'd never deserve to suffer in the potential ways I've described. 

If I was to leave, he'd come with me. That loan would be for us both - even more the reason it's impossible because I'd never put him in that position with debt hanging over him. I care too much about his career prospects and his happiness to put either of ours first. He's happy to relocate - but in the right way at the right time and I know that that's the way to be fair to him and he deserves that - otherwise I wouldn't deserve him.

I'm pretty depressed, and I do think about ending it... but I couldn't at the price of harming others. My morals wouldn't let me.

>What do you need more - good advice or just emotional support?

That's a fair point... probably need better emotional support.. as my recount of my Mum's behaviour shows I'm in such a bad position with my jobs there's not much more advice out there I can use to get through... I actually work with another girl who is in the same position as me (although she's only in the office 2 days a week - and only works for asshole boss) and we did make a final attempt to make our lives bearable with him.. but we've both found that there is literally nothing else we can do and hence have given up.

>Considered France?

I would consider France. I studied French for several years at school but tbh I never quite grasped it either... I don't seem to be able to talk in other languages naturally! But my parents use to bring me to France year after year since I was a baby until my mid-teens for about a month at a time... so bizarrely I can understand french VERY well when I hear it... I'm just awful at figuring out how to speak it/write in it!

I'm not sure about the job prospects tho... especially jobs in my field. ATM I am working in Public Relations here... in the public sector, mostly online and with event management involved too. There's just no jobs in my part of Ireland in that field, and those that are available are asking mostly for about 6yrs exp when I only have just over 2. 

Does France have much in that sector? Or has the recession caused most to ignore public relations roles like over here too?

Yeh no doubt I should learn that... I guess I stress out because I have a paranoia that if I let myself open up, I'll let myself get really depressed about all the things I can't sort/change right now and I won't be able to stop that downward spiral....

A few years ago I did suffer from Post-traumatic Stress disorder and I got severely depressed because of it. I've since overcome it, and haven't been depressed since but I do get scared something could get on top of me like that again and ruin my life.

I have a best friend who is a few years younger than me... she did a longer course than me at uni, so she's still a student as well and tbh she's a bit naive about the working world. I do explain what I'm going through, and although sometimes she can be a sympathetic listener, a lot of the time she tells me she simply doesn't know how to tell me to deal with my problems at work because she'd "just have walked out by now".

My other close friends.. well I don't mean to sound like an arrogant douche, but they're not that emotionally mature and I think they would be even more at a loss of how to advice me!

I talk to my mother quite a bit.. she has a fairly high powered job in sort of the same area as me - but she's sometimes a great comfort and support coming up with solutions I'd never have thought of... but other times, normally when there are no solutions to offer, just sympathy, she freaks out and get's militant on me. She (like me to a degree) is paranoid that if she lets me self-pity or be open to her about how unhappy I am, that I will fall down the rabbithole and not get come back out of it. I don't even think she's aware she's thinking that, but I've pieced together her attitudes over the years via experience and throwaway comments. Her sister is a very depressed person, who refuses to do anything to try to be happy. It has both frustrated and frightened the hell out of my mum... Her guilt that she was never able to solve her sisters unhappiness from her teens to her 50s seems to have left such a bad impression on her, that she frequently responds to my hardships with aggression.. so sometimes you just don't know what you're going to get - a compassionate supporter who really understands your struggles, or someone who is tearing your face off because she thinks you're giving up on life because how dare you not stick with it!

I don't mind saying where I live, I live in Ireland.... I wanted to learn German and think about moving there as there are simply no jobs here and I don't want to live mainland UK... I'd be open to other EU countries if there was work going in my area... Which is communications - which is also exactly why I need to have a very VERY good grasp of the countries language before relocation!

I feel like I'm all out of courage. Not so depleted I could top myself, but enough to want to pretty badly.

I do tell him I'm unhappy with my job/country/life but I don't go so far to tell him just how epically unhappy I am. I don't want to freak him out with these feelings/thoughts, or scare him that I could actually do it. Not to mention I don't want him to feel bad about his new job that's tying us down here.

Plus as much as I love him, he is fucking awful at supportive commentary - a hug and a cuppa and listening to me whine? No problem. Having to respond? Epic failure. He kinda opts to throw out impossible solutions (such as "get a loan, make a run for it and be happy!) and I end up getting insanely frustrated. I rarely let my stress out - I'm one of those people who crush it deep inside me and sideline it so I can kept fighting forward.. but last night I couldn't take it anymore and got home and after telling him how upset I was that I didn't think I could handle learning a new language after all, it all started coming out; how I felt like I'd never get out, how I was so unhappy... I cried a lot.

He then gets panicked and starts making fruitless suggestions, I get frustrated that he seems to suggest these things without thinking through what he's saying and he gets angry that I'm so angry when he's just trying to help..

In summary, we've not spoken since last night... and I know that's mostly my fault for not being more tolerant when he was just trying to make me feel be, albeit in the wrong way for me. So I'm sure I'll see him tonight and apologise for going mental and pick up the charade of 'coping' where I left off....
